es: Reconocer y usar ecos (Did you?, Have you?) y fichas como Fair enough o No way! para mostrar interés, sorpresa o aceptación, y distinguirlos de las question tags.

teaching.en: "I've joined a choir." "Have you? Since when?"
teaching.es: «Me he apuntado a un coro.» «¿Ah, sí? ¿Desde cuándo?»
teaching.explanationEs: Have you? repite el auxiliar de I've: es un eco que muestra interés, no pide un dato.
teaching.audioText: "I've joined a choir." "Have you? Since when?"

teaching.en: "She got the promotion." "Did she? Good for her!"
teaching.es: «Consiguió el ascenso.» «¿Sí? ¡Me alegro por ella!»
teaching.explanationEs: Got es pasado simple, así que el eco usa did. Después del eco se añade un comentario.
teaching.audioText: "She got the promotion." "Did she? Good for her!"

teaching.en: "You've met my colleague, haven't you?" "I have, yes. She seems nice."
teaching.es: «Ya conoces a mi colega, ¿verdad?» «Sí, la conozco. Parece simpática.»
teaching.explanationEs: La tag haven't you? pide confirmar algo que el hablante ya cree; el eco Have you? reacciona a una noticia.
teaching.audioText: "You've met my colleague, haven't you?" "I have, yes. She seems nice."

teaching.en: "Honestly, I found the film too long." "Fair enough. I got a bit bored too."
teaching.es: «Sinceramente, la película se me hizo larga.» «Vale, te entiendo. A mí también me aburrió un poco.»
teaching.explanationEs: Fair enough acepta la opinión del otro sin discutirla.
segments: "Honestly, I found the film too long." "Fair
enough. I got a bit bored too."
teaching.audioText: "Honestly, I found the film too long." "Fair enough. I got a bit bored too."

teaching.en: "I'm running a marathon in May." "No way! Since when do you run?"
teaching.es: «Voy a correr un maratón en mayo.» «¡No puede ser! ¿Desde cuándo corres?»
teaching.explanationEs: No way! expresa incredulidad o admiración; el contexto decide cuál.
segments: way! Since when do you run?"
teaching.audioText: "I'm running a marathon in May." "No way! Since when do you run?"

teaching.en: "Guess what? I've got a job offer in Lisbon." "Have you? That's brilliant!"
teaching.es: «¿A que no sabes qué? Me han hecho una oferta de trabajo en Lisboa.» «¿Ah, sí? ¡Qué bien!»
teaching.explanationEs: Guess what? abre un tema con una noticia; el eco Have you? reacciona a ella.
segments: "Guess what? I've got a job offer
teaching.audioText: "Guess what? I've got a job offer in Lisbon." "Have you? That's brilliant!"

prompt.es: Completa el eco: «Sam y Ana se han mudado a Leeds.» — «¿Ah, sí? ¿Cuándo?»

feedback.es: La frase original usa have (have moved), y el eco repite ese auxiliar con el pronombre they: Have they?

hint.es: Fíjate en el auxiliar de la frase original y repítelo con un pronombre.

origin.text: "Sam and Ana have moved to Leeds." "___ they? When?"

prompt.es: ¿Qué eco repite el auxiliar y la polaridad para mostrar interés?

feedback.es: La frase es negativa y en pasado: didn't. El eco repite ese auxiliar con la misma polaridad. Did she? suena a duda y Doesn't she? cambia el tiempo.

hint.es: Busca el auxiliar de la frase original y mantén que es negativa.

origin.text: "She didn't like the film."

prompt.es: Ordena: «Vale, te entiendo. A mí tampoco me gustó mucho.»

answer.text: Fair enough. I didn't like it much either.

feedback.es: Fair enough acepta la opinión del otro y either añade que tú piensas lo mismo en una frase negativa.

hint.es: Primero la ficha que acepta la opinión; después tu frase negativa.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada intervención con lo que hace el hablante.

The second speaker changes the subject.

prompt.es: Completa los tres ecos: no come, esperamos, ganó.

feedback.es: Cada eco repite el auxiliar de su frase: doesn't (negativa), have (have been waiting) y did (pasado de won).

He asks Mia to agree with him.

The second speaker shows interest and asks why.

es: Usar encabezamientos (That film, it was brilliant) y colas (She's lovely, your sister) con el pronombre obligatorio y concordante, como en la gramática oral.

teaching.en: That film, it was absolutely brilliant.
teaching.es: Esa película, fue absolutamente genial.
teaching.explanationEs: Cabeza: el tema va primero y un pronombre (it) lo retoma.
teaching.audioText: That film, it was absolutely brilliant.

teaching.en: Your sister, she's so lovely.
teaching.es: Tu hermana, qué encantadora es.
teaching.explanationEs: El pronombre concuerda con el nombre: sister → she.
teaching.audioText: Your sister, she's so lovely.

teaching.en: She's a great cook, your mum.
teaching.es: Es una gran cocinera, tu madre.
teaching.explanationEs: Cola: la frase completa va primero y el tema se añade al final.
teaching.audioText: She's a great cook, your mum.

teaching.en: They're never quiet, my neighbours.
teaching.es: Nunca están callados, mis vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: Con un nombre plural, la cola usa they: neighbours → they're.
teaching.audioText: They're never quiet, my neighbours.

teaching.en: It's a bit noisy, that café, isn't it?
teaching.es: Es un poco ruidoso, ese café, ¿verdad?
teaching.explanationEs: Con cola, la tag va al final y copia el auxiliar de la frase: It's → isn't it.
teaching.audioText: It's a bit noisy, that café, isn't it?

teaching.en: I can't stand him, that manager.
teaching.es: No lo soporto, ese jefe.
teaching.explanationEs: Si el tema es el objeto, la cola usa him, her o them: I can't stand him.
teaching.audioText: I can't stand him, that manager.

prompt.es: Ordena con cabeza: «Mi hermano, es cocinero.»

feedback.es: La cabeza coloca el tema primero y el pronombre he lo retoma antes del comentario.

hint.es: El tema va primero; después el pronombre y el comentario.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese café, siempre era ruidoso.»

feedback.es: El pronombre it retoma a café, que es una cosa en singular.

hint.es: Es un lugar, no una persona, y está en singular.

origin.text: That café, ___ was always noisy.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase lleva bien la cabeza y el pronombre?

feedback.es: Tras la cabeza hace falta un pronombre que concuerde: brother pide he. Sin pronombre la frase queda coja y con she no concuerda.

hint.es: El pronombre es obligatorio y debe ser masculino.

prompt.es: Elige la cola con el pronombre y la tag correctos.

They're rather expensive, that restaurant, isn't it?

feedback.es: Restaurant es singular y cosa: it, y la tag repite el auxiliar de It's: isn't it. They're o aren't they no concuerdan.

accepted: He lives in Paris, my cousin.

es: Recuperar lo que se omite o se sustituye en réplicas rápidas (I'd love to, So have I, Neither did she, I hope so, I'm afraid not).

teaching.en: "Would you like to come to the wedding?" "I'd love to. Thanks for the invitation."
teaching.es: «¿Te gustaría venir a la boda?» «Me encantaría. Gracias por la invitación.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd love to omite el verbo que ya se dijo (come): solo queda to.
segments: "Would you like to come to the wedding?"
"I'd love to. Thanks for the invitation."
teaching.audioText: "Would you like to come to the wedding?" "I'd love to. Thanks for the invitation."

teaching.en: "I'm exhausted." "So am I."
teaching.es: «Estoy agotado.» «Yo también.»
teaching.explanationEs: So + auxiliar + sujeto = yo también. El auxiliar es el de la frase original: am.
teaching.audioText: "I'm exhausted." "So am I."

teaching.en: "I didn't sleep well." "Neither did I."
teaching.es: «No dormí bien.» «Yo tampoco.»
teaching.explanationEs: Neither + auxiliar + sujeto = yo tampoco; el verbo se omite y el auxiliar copia didn't.
teaching.audioText: "I didn't sleep well." "Neither did I."

teaching.en: "Will the tickets be cheap?" "I hope so."
teaching.es: «¿Serán baratas las entradas?» «Espero que sí.»
teaching.explanationEs: So sustituye a toda la oración (the tickets will be cheap). En negativo: I hope not.
teaching.audioText: "Will the tickets be cheap?" "I hope so."

teaching.en: "Is the restaurant still open?" "I'm afraid not."
teaching.es: «¿Sigue abierto el restaurante?» «Me temo que no.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid not da una mala noticia con educación y sustituye a «it isn't open».
teaching.audioText: "Is the restaurant still open?" "I'm afraid not."

teaching.en: "Shall we walk home?" "I'd rather not. It's late."
teaching.es: «¿Volvemos andando?» «Prefiero que no. Es tarde.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather not omite el verbo de la propuesta (walk home).
teaching.audioText: "Shall we walk home?" "I'd rather not. It's late."

feedback.es: I'd love to omite el verbo ya mencionado (come) y deja solo to.

hint.es: Es la partícula del infinitivo omitido.

hint.es: Busca neither + auxiliar + sujeto, copiando el auxiliar de la frase.

es: Redactar un intercambio natural con marcadores de discurso (anyway, by the way, to be honest, come to think of it, actually) y una question tag.

teaching.en: Anyway, let's get back to the plan for Saturday.
teaching.es: En fin, volvamos al plan del sábado.
teaching.explanationEs: Anyway vuelve al tema principal después de una digresión.
teaching.audioText: Anyway, let's get back to the plan for Saturday.

teaching.en: By the way, did you remember to call the landlord?
teaching.es: Por cierto, ¿te acordaste de llamar al casero?
teaching.explanationEs: By the way introduce un tema nuevo que se te acaba de ocurrir.
teaching.audioText: By the way, did you remember to call the landlord?

teaching.en: To be honest, I found the first half a bit slow.
teaching.es: Para ser sincero, la primera parte me pareció algo lenta.
teaching.explanationEs: To be honest suaviza una opinión sincera; no se dice «to say the truth».
segments: To be honest, I found the

teaching.en: Come to think of it, didn't Mia mention that idea last week?

segments: Come to think of it, didn't
Mia mention that idea last week?

segments: Actually, I'd prefer to meet at

prompt.es: Escribe un intercambio de unas 120 palabras con los marcadores pedidos.

answer.text:
Tom: So, are we having dinner at your place on Saturday?
Mia: To be honest, I'd rather not cook this time. My oven is broken, and I'm exhausted after work.
Tom: Fair enough. We could order pizza, couldn't we?
Mia: Good idea. By the way, did you see Sara's new flat? It's lovely.
Tom: Not yet. Is it big? I hope so, because we are a large group.
Mia: Quite big. Anyway, about Saturday: is seven o'clock all right for you?
Tom: Perfect. Come to think of it, Leo and Ana are free that night too. Shall we invite them?
Mia: Yes, let's do that. I'll text them now and tell them to bring some dessert.
accepted:
Tom: So, are we having dinner at your place on Saturday?
Mia: To be honest, I'd rather not cook this time. My oven is broken, and I'm exhausted after work.
Tom: Fair enough. We could order pizza, couldn't we?
Mia: Good idea. By the way, did you see Sara's new flat? It's lovely.
Tom: Not yet. Is it big? I hope so, because we are a large group.
Mia: Quite big. Anyway, about Saturday: is seven o'clock all right for you?
Tom: Perfect. Come to think of it, Leo and Ana are free that night too. Shall we invite them?
Mia: Yes, let's do that. I'll text them now and tell them to bring some dessert.

Tom: Are we meeting at your flat on Saturday?
Mia: Honestly, I'd rather go out. My kitchen is a mess, and I've got no time to clean it.
Tom: No problem. Let's book a table somewhere, shall we?
Mia: Sure. By the way, did you know Sara has a new flat? It's very lovely, apparently.
Tom: No way! Since when?
Mia: Since last month. Anyway, what time suits you on Saturday? Seven?
Tom: Seven is fine, although I might be a bit late. Actually, come to think of it, Leo wants to come too, doesn't he? I'll ask him tonight.
Mia: Good. Then we are four, and I'll book the table for eight o'clock. Is that all right with you?

feedback.es: Un buen intercambio vuelve al plan con anyway, cambia de tema con by the way, opina con to be honest, recuerda con come to think of it y usa una tag.
